prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a hit while turning left in League City, Texas, and has shoulder injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1263; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded for claim purposes. Can you please state your full name for the record?

A: I'd rather just go by the claimant on this one, if that's okay. I'm the driver of the vehicle involved.

Q: That's fine. Can you walk me through what happened at the intersection in League City?

A: I was making a left turn off the main road into the shopping center. I had my turn signal on and I was waiting for a gap in oncoming traffic. When I saw a clear spot, I started to turn, and that's when another car came through and hit the front passenger side of my vehicle.

Q: Had the oncoming vehicle been stopped at the light, or was it moving at the time?

A: It was moving. It wasn't speeding that I could tell, but it didn't look like it slowed down much either.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before you started your turn?

A: I saw headlights a ways back. I thought I had enough time, and I misjudged it. I'll own that part.

Q: How are you feeling now? Have you been seen by a medical provider?

A: My right shoulder is pretty bad. It hit the door frame when the airbag went off. I went to an urgent care clinic that same day and they took X-rays. I've got a follow-up with an orthopedic doctor next week because the pain hasn't gone away and I can barely lift my arm above my head.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add about the accident?

A: Just that I'm cooperating fully and I have the photos I took at the scene. I can send them over whenever you need.

Q: Thank you for your time. We'll be in touch with next steps.
